proposal.title: Report: Russian Contacts Requested U.S. Financial Information Through Unofficial Emails
proposal.description_short: TPM reported that Russian government contacts requested U.S. citizens’ financial information from Treasury officials through unofficial email accounts.
proposal.description_medium: In December 2018, Talking Points Memo summarized BuzzFeed News reporting that Russian government contacts requested financial information about U.S. citizens from Treasury officials through unofficial email accounts. TPM quoted a FinCEN official expressing concern about the communications. The article says it was unclear how much, if any, information was exchanged; it does not establish an unauthorized disclosure or a Russian infiltration of Treasury.
proposal.description_long: A December 2018 Talking Points Memo article summarized BuzzFeed News reporting about requests for U.S. citizens’ financial information sent to Treasury officials by Russian government contacts through unofficial email accounts. TPM said some Treasury officials were unaware of communications that did not use a secure network, and it quoted a Financial Crimes Enforcement Network official who raised concern about what information might be passed to Russian contacts. TPM also reported that the Russian side was interested in information about at least two dozen people, including dissidents, academics and private investigators. The article explicitly left unclear how much information, or what information, was exchanged. This supports an attributed account of requests and concern about their handling. It does not show that officials disclosed records, that Russia accessed Treasury systems, or that the department was infiltrated. TPM attributed its report to BuzzFeed, so the claim should remain framed as reported information rather than an official finding.

proposal.title: Prosecutors Cited Trump’s Posts in Seeking a Discovery Protective Order
proposal.description_short: Prosecutors cited Trump’s posts when seeking limits on disclosure of discovery evidence in the 2020 election case.
proposal.description_medium: In August 2023, prosecutors in the federal 2020 election case asked a Washington judge to set rules for Donald Trump and his lawyers when reviewing discovery materials, citing Trump’s prior social-media posts about his cases. A separate September request sought a narrow gag order on attacks against case participants; Trump’s attorneys argued he needed to remain free to campaign. These were requests and arguments, not a judicial finding that the posts were crimes.
proposal.description_long: In August 2023, the Justice Department asked a federal judge in Washington to impose rules on Donald Trump and his attorneys as they reviewed discovery materials in the federal case over the 2020 election. The Washington Post reported that prosecutors cited Trump’s history of discussing cases on social media when explaining their request. That discovery protective-order request concerned how evidence would be handled; it should not be confused with a general ban on public statements. In a separate September 2023 filing, prosecutors sought a narrow gag order barring attacks on participants in the case. The Washington Post reported that Trump’s attorneys opposed that request and argued he needed to remain free to campaign for the Republican nomination. These sources document requests and legal arguments at different points in the case. They do not establish that the posts were criminal, that a court adopted every restriction prosecutors sought, or that the two filings were one proceeding or order.

proposal.title: Trump Announced His 2024 Presidential Campaign at Mar-a-Lago
proposal.description_short: Donald Trump announced his 2024 presidential campaign at Mar-a-Lago on November 15, 2022.
proposal.description_medium: Reuters reported that Donald Trump announced his 2024 presidential campaign at Mar-a-Lago on November 15, 2022, one week after the midterm elections. proposal.description_long: Donald Trump announced that he would seek the presidency again in 2024 at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Florida, on November 15, 2022. Reuters reported that he made the announcement one week after the midterm elections, in which Republicans did not win as many seats in Congress as they had hoped. The report described the campaign as a bid to regain the presidency and said Trump aimed to pre-empt potential Republican rivals. Trump’s announcement began a campaign for the Republican nomination, with the formal selection process still ahead. This proposed account reports the event and attributes the political context to Reuters’ contemporaneous coverage. It does not infer that the announcement was designed to influence a criminal or civil case, shield Trump from prosecution, or affect any court proceeding. The cited report supports the campaign launch, date, venue and stated political context; claims about an undisclosed legal motive would require separate evidence.
